flagshipTools.name: InfraDispatch
flagshipTools.problem: Pickup points, vehicle fit, team handovers and approval details are often fragmented across messages and spreadsheets.
flagshipTools.user: DMC transport coordinators, dispatch supervisors and destination operations teams
flagshipTools.inputs: Trip, pickup points, guest load, team, vehicle, costs and approvals
flagshipTools.output: Route logic, operational briefing, Google Maps links and print-ready manifest
flagshipTools.context: Browser-hosted static MVP using operating rules and mock/reference data.
flagshipTools.logic: Applies transparent rules to pickup pressure, zones, guest load, vehicle suitability, readiness and handover completeness.
flagshipTools.demonstrates: How an operational brief can be assembled consistently before dispatch.
flagshipTools.limitations: No live fleet telemetry, driver app, traffic API, authentication or production database.
flagshipTools.next: Validated API integrations, role-based approvals and live dispatch status.

flagshipTools.name: InfraCluster
flagshipTools.problem: Large hotel pickup programmes create avoidable route, timing, language and capacity conflicts.
flagshipTools.user: MICE movement controllers, hotel-desk teams and transport planners
flagshipTools.inputs: Hotel groups, zones, timing, language, passenger load, vehicle fit and cost signals
flagshipTools.output: Suggested pickup clusters, operational review flags and dispatch handoff data
flagshipTools.context: Static browser MVP for educational planning and supervisor review.
flagshipTools.logic: Groups compatible pickups using visible timing, zone, load and service constraints.
flagshipTools.demonstrates: How clustering rules can expose pressure before coaches are assigned.
flagshipTools.limitations: No road-network optimization, live traffic, supplier inventory or perfect-route claim.
flagshipTools.next: Route-engine integration and controlled comparison against dispatcher decisions.
flagshipTools.relatedTitle: From Hotel Lobby to Coach Door

flagshipTools.name: InfraSky
flagshipTools.problem: Stargazing products are sometimes sold without a consistent check of sky, access, product promise and operating readiness.
flagshipTools.user: Destination managers, product teams, desert operators and experience planners
flagshipTools.inputs: Location, date, guest profile, equipment, guide level, product promise and condition assumptions
flagshipTools.output: Readiness signal, operating timeline, team briefings and exportable planning payloads
flagshipTools.context: Condition-aware static MVP with illustrative/reference data, not a safety or weather authority.
flagshipTools.logic: Combines transparent product-fit and readiness rules into an explainable operating signal.
flagshipTools.demonstrates: How responsible product decisions can connect sales promises to field readiness.
flagshipTools.limitations: No guaranteed forecast, permit confirmation, emergency authority or live supplier status.
flagshipTools.next: Verified weather/astronomy feeds and destination-specific governance controls.

flagshipTools.name: InfraQuote
flagshipTools.problem: Tour quotations can hide cost classification, break-even and margin risk behind a final selling price.
flagshipTools.user: DMC sales, product, costing and quotation-review teams
flagshipTools.inputs: Service assumptions, fixed/variable/conditional costs, guests, margin or markup, VAT and terms
flagshipTools.output: Cost worksheet, price, profit, break-even, readiness review and client quotation
flagshipTools.context: Static browser MVP with user-entered assumptions and no live supplier rates.
flagshipTools.logic: Uses documented commercial formulas and visible review thresholds.
flagshipTools.demonstrates: How pricing economics and operational readiness can be reviewed together.
flagshipTools.limitations: Not an accounting, tax, ERP or supplier-contract system; entered rates require user verification.
flagshipTools.next: Controlled rate libraries, approvals and production quotation records.
flagshipTools.relatedTitle: Net Cost, Selling Price, Markup and Margin

labTools.name: Vehicle Requirement Calculator
labTools.problem: Estimate a defensible minimum and operational vehicle count without treating nominal seat capacity as usable capacity.
labTools.user: Transport coordinators, DMC operations and group planners
labTools.inputs: Passengers, nominal capacity, luggage profile, accessibility seat allowance and spare-capacity target
labTools.output: Effective capacity, minimum vehicles, recommended vehicles, spare seats and occupancy

labTools.name: MICE Arrival Wave Planner
labTools.problem: Turn several flight arrivals into visible operating waves, vehicle demand, meet-and-greet demand and hotel splits.
labTools.user: MICE controllers, airport teams and transport planners
labTools.inputs: Flight reference, arrival time, passengers, hotel, vehicle capacity, meet capacity and grouping window
labTools.output: Arrival waves, time spans, holding periods, vehicle requirements, meet teams and hotel split
labTools.relatedTitle: Before the Delegate Reaches the Hotel

labTools.name: Guide Allocation Planner
labTools.problem: Make language, availability and schedule conflicts visible before guide assignments are confirmed.
labTools.user: Tour operations coordinators, guide supervisors and destination teams
labTools.inputs: Groups, language, guest load, start, duration, location and guide availability
labTools.output: Suggested assignments, conflicts, unassigned groups and schedule coverage

labTools.name: Guest Journey Mapper
labTools.problem: Connect guest expectations, ownership, risk, measures and improvement opportunities across the complete experience.
labTools.user: Destination managers, experience designers, quality teams and hotel/tour operators
labTools.inputs: Stage, touchpoint, expectation, owner, risk, KPI and improvement opportunity
labTools.output: Visual journey, risk summary and CSV-ready improvement register
labTools.resourceTitle: Connect journey mapping to SOP design

labTools.name: SOP Structure Builder
labTools.problem: Turn an operating process into a controlled first-draft structure before detailed procedure writing begins.
labTools.user: Process owners, quality managers, supervisors and operations professionals
labTools.inputs: Process, objective, scope, roles, trigger, steps, controls, escalation and records
labTools.output: Structured SOP outline ready to copy, review or print
labTools.relatedTitle: How to Write a Professional SOP Structure
